draft.title: Physical aids
card: Protective equipment
gear worn to shield the body from impact or harm, such as helmets, mouthguards and shin guards.
Taping
tape applied around a joint or muscle to give extra support and limit movements that could cause injury. Athletes often use it on ankles and fingers.
Brace
a firm support worn around a joint, such as the knee or ankle. It steadies the joint and limits unwanted movement.
These aids reduce the risk of injury, and taping and braces can also support a joint that was hurt before. They do not remove the risk completely.
draft.remember: Protective gear, tape and braces support the body and reduce injury risk, but do not remove it.

a.q: Why might a netballer with a weak ankle wear a brace?
opts: To steady the joint and limit unwanted movement
To warm the muscles before the game starts
To restore strength after an injury
To make the ankle completely safe from injury
a.why: A brace supports a joint and limits movement that could cause injury. It cannot make the ankle completely safe, because aids reduce risk but do not remove it.
a.clue: Think about what a brace does to the joint.

b.q: Sam plays cricket and wears a helmet when batting against fast bowlers. Which statement about the helmet is most accurate?
opts: It reduces the risk of a head injury from the ball
It removes any chance of a head injury
It supports a joint by limiting its movement
It prepares the muscles for harder work
b.why: Protective equipment shields the body from impact, so it lowers the risk of injury. It cannot remove the risk completely. Supporting a joint is the job of taping and braces.
b.clue: Aids lower risk, but they do not make it zero.

a.best: To steady the joint and limit unwanted movement

b.best: It reduces the risk of a head injury from the ball

problems.detail: The clue 'Aids lower risk, but they do not make it zero' points straight at the 'reduces the risk' option and rules out 'removes any chance'. The other two distractors are plainly off-topic for a helmet, so a student can answer without knowing the idea.

b.q: Priya, a hockey goalkeeper, wears leg pads. She also tapes an ankle she sprained last season. Which statement is most accurate?
opts: Tape supports her ankle, and pads shield her from impact
Pads support her ankle, and tape shields her from impact
Tape and pads together remove her risk of injury
Tape helps her only because her ankle was hurt before
b.why: Taping supports a joint and limits risky movement, while pads are protective equipment that shield the body from impact. Tape is not only for a past injury: it can also help prevent a first one. No aid removes the risk completely.
b.clue: Match each aid to the job it does.

a.best: To steady the joint and limit unwanted movement

b.best: Tape supports her ankle, and pads shield her from impact
